title: Real Estate Lead Management: Process, Stages, CRM and Follow-Up

faqs.question: What is real estate lead management?
faqs.answer: It is the process of capturing every property enquiry in one place, replying within minutes, qualifying the buyer, following up until each lead books a site visit or says no, and measuring which sources bring site visits and bookings, not just enquiries.

faqs.question: What are the steps in real estate lead management?
faqs.answer: Capture every enquiry with its source, acknowledge it instantly, assign it to one salesperson, call and qualify, book a site visit with two time options, follow up with a next action and date, and measure results by source every week, sending outcomes back to the ad platforms.

faqs.question: What are the main types of real estate leads?
faqs.answer: By source: Meta lead forms, Google search ads, website forms, WhatsApp click-to-chat, property portals, channel partners, and referrals and walk-ins. By readiness: hot, warm, cold and closed. Each source behaves differently, so record it on every lead and compare sources by site visits, not volume.

faqs.question: How quickly should I respond to a real estate lead?
faqs.answer: Within minutes if possible, and within an hour at most. A 2011 Harvard Business Review study found firms that contacted online leads within an hour were nearly seven times as likely to qualify them as firms that waited longer. An instant WhatsApp reply plus a call from a person works well.

faqs.question: What is a CRM in real estate?
faqs.answer: Software that stores every lead with its source, stage, notes, calls, messages and next action, and reminds the team what to do each day. A good real estate CRM also schedules site visits, reports by source and salesperson, and sends qualified leads and visits back to Meta and Google.

faqs.question: Can I manage real estate leads in Excel or Google Sheets?
faqs.answer: Yes, to start. A shared sheet with columns for source, stage, next action, next date and owner works for a small broker. Once leads arrive from several sources or more than two or three people handle them, a CRM with automatic capture and reminders stops leads getting lost.

faqs.question: What lead stages should a real estate team use?
faqs.answer: New, contacted, qualified, visit booked, visit done, negotiation or EOI, and booked or closed with a reason. Every lead should sit in exactly one stage with a next action and a date, so the team always knows what to do today.

faqs.question: What should a real estate sales team measure?
faqs.answer: Time to first reply, leads with no contact after 24 hours, conversion from lead to qualified to site visit to booking by source, cost per site visit and per booking for each campaign, and the reasons leads were closed, so you can fix targeting.
